questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the area of a loop of the curve $\mathrm{r}=\operatorname{asin} 3 \theta$ ?
questions.solution:
If curve $\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{a} \sin 3 \theta$ To trace the curve, we consider the following table : $\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline$3 $\theta=$& 0 & $\frac{\pi}{2}$& $\pi$& $\frac{3 \pi}{2}$& 2 $\pi$& $\frac{5 \pi}{2}$& 3 $\pi$\\ \hline$\theta=$& 0 & $\frac{\pi}{6}$& $\frac{\pi}{3}$& $\frac{\pi}{2}$& $\frac{2 \pi}{3}$& $\frac{5 \pi}{6}$& $\pi$\\ \hline $\mathrm{r}=$& 0 & $\mathrm{a}$& 0 & -$\mathrm{a}$& 0 & $\mathrm{a}$& 0 \\ \hline \end{array} Thus there is a loop between $\theta=0 \& \theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$ as r varies from $\mathrm{r}=0$ to $\mathrm{r}=0$.
Hence, the area of the loop lying in the $\text{ positive quadrant }=\frac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}$r^{2} $\mathrm{~d} \theta =\frac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \sin ^{2} \phi \cdot \frac{1}{3} \mathrm{~d} \phi\left[\right.$ On putting, $\left.3 \theta=\phi \Rightarrow \mathrm{d} \theta=\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{~d} \phi\right]$ $\begin{array}{c} =$$\frac{a^{2}}{6} \int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \sin ^{2} \phi \mathrm{d} \phi$\\ =$\frac{\mathrma^{2}}{6} \cdot \int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{1-\cos 2 \phi}{2} \mathrm{~d} \phi\left[\because \cos$2 $\theta=$1-2 \sin ^{2} $\theta\right] \end{array}=\frac{\mathrma^{2}}{12} \cdot\left[\phi+\frac{\sin 2 \phi}{2}\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}=\frac{\mathrma^{2}}{12} \cdot\left[\frac{\pi}{2}+\sin \pi\right]=\frac{\mathrma^{2} \pi}{24}$

questions.q: For which of the following values of $\mathrm{m}$, the area of the region bounded by the curve $y=x-x^{2}$ and the line $y=m x$ equals $\frac{9}{2}$
questions.solution: The equation of curve is $y=x-x^{2}\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow x^{2}-x=y \\ \Rightarrow\left(x-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}=- \lleft(y-\frac{1}{4}\right) \end{array}which is a parabola whose vertex is \left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{4}\right)$ \\ Hence, finding the point of intersection of the curve and the line, $x-x^{2}=m x \Rightarrow x(1-x-m)=0$ i.e., $x=0$ or $x=1-m\therefore \frac{9}{2}=\int_{0}^{1-\mathrm{m}}\left(\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{x}^{2}-\mathrm{mx}\right) \mathrm{dx}= \left\{\frac{x^{2}}{2}-\frac{x^{3}}{3}-$m $\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right$\}_{0}^{1-m}=(1-$\mathrm{m}) \frac{(1-\mathrm{m})^{2}}{2}-\frac{(1-\mathrm{m})^{3}}{3}=\frac{(1-\mathrm{m})^{3}}{6}\therefore(1-$\$mathrm{m})^{3}=\frac{6 \times 9}{2}=27\Rightarrow 1-\mathrm{m}=(27)^{1 / 3}=3\Rightarrow \mathrm{m}=-2$ Also, $(1-\mathrm{m})^{3}-(3)^{3}=0\therefore(1-\mathrm{m})^{3}=3^{3} \Rightarrow 1-\mathrm{m}=3$ or $\mathrm{m}=$-$2$$

questions.q: If $(x+y) \sin u=x^{2} y^{2}$, then $x \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+y \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=$
questions.solution:
Given : $(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}) \sin \mathrm{U}=\mathrmx^{2} \mathrmy^{2}\Rightarrow \sin \mathrm{U}=\frac{\mathrmx^{2} \mathrmy^{2}}{\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}}=\mathrm{v}(\mathrm{let})$
Here $\mathrm{n}=2-1=1$
Euler's theorem $\mathrm{x} \cdot \frac{\partial \mathrm{v}}{\partial \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{y} \cdot \frac{\partial \mathrm{v}}{\partial \mathrm{y}}=\mathrm{nv}\therefore \mathrm{x} \frac{\partial \sin \mathrm{U}}{\partial \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{y} \frac{\partial \sin \mathrm{U}}{\partial \mathrm{y}}=\sin \mathrm{U}\Rightarrow \mathrm{x} \cdot \cos \mathrm{U} \frac{\partial \mathrm{U}}{\partial \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{y} \cdot \cos \mathrm{U} \cdot \frac{\partial \mathrm{U}}{\partial \mathrm{y}}=\sin \mathrm{U}\Rightarrow \mathrm{x} \frac{\partial \mathrm{U}}{\partial \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{y} \frac{\partial \mathrm{U}}{\partial \mathrm{y}}=\frac{\sin \mathrm{U}}{\cos \mathrm{U}}=\tan \mathrm{U}\Rightarrow \mathrm{x} \frac{\partial \mathrm{U}}{\partial \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{y} \frac{\partial \mathrm{U}}{\partial \mathrm{y}}=\tan \mathrm{U}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The function $f(x)=x^{2} e^{-2 x}, x > 0$. Then the maximum value of $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{l}
\text{ Given : } \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}^{2} \mathrm{e}^{-2 \mathrm{x}}, \mathrm{x} > 0 \\
\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}^{2} \cdot \mathrm{e}^{-2 \mathrm{x}}(-2)+\mathrm{e}^{-2 \mathrm{x}} \cdot 2 \mathrm{x} \\
\text{ put } \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=0 \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{e}^{-2 \mathrm{x}} \cdot \mathrm{x}(-\mathrm{x}+1)=0 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=1 \text{ or } \mathrm{x}=0 \\
\mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=\left(-4 \mathrm{x}^{2}-6 \mathrm{x}+1\right) \mathrm{e}^{-2 \mathrm{x}} \\
\mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(1)=-9 \mathrm{e}^{-2 \mathrm{x}} < 0 \\
\mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(0)=\mathrm{e}^{-2 \mathrm{x}} > 0 \\
\therefore \text{ value of } \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}) \text{ is maximum at } \mathrm{x}=1 \\
\because \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}^{2} \cdot \mathrm{e}^{-2 \mathrm{x}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(1)=\mathrm{e}^{-2}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}^{2}}
\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In rolling two fair dice, what is the probability of obtaining a sum greater than 3 but not exceeding $6 ?$
questions.solution:
Let $S$ be the sample space
$\because \mathrm{n}(\mathrm{S})=36$
Events
[sum greater than 3 but not exceeding 6]
$\begin{array}{l}
=\{(2,2),(3,1),(1,3),(4,1),(1,4),(5,1)(1,5) \\
(3,2),(2,3),(4,2),(2,4),(3,3)\} \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}(\mathrm{E})=12 \\
\therefore \text{ Required probability }=\frac{\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{E})}{\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{S})}=\frac{12}{36}=\frac{1}{3}
\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $Team A has probability \frac{2}{3}$ of winning whenever it plays. Suppose A plays four games. What is the probability that A wins more than half of its games?
questions.solution:
Let ' $\mathrm{p}$ ' denote the probability of winning of team A whenever it plays
$\therefore \mathrm{p}=\frac{2}{3} \ \text{ and } \mathrm{q}=1-\frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$
Let $X$ denotes the number of winning games out of 4 games i.e. $n=4\therefore$ The probability of $r$ success $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}=\mathrm{r})={ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{c}_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrmp^{\mathrm{r}} \mathrmq^{\mathrm{n}-\mathrm{r}}, \mathrm{r}=0,1,2,3,4\therefore$ Probability of winning more than half games $=\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X} > 2)=\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}=3)+\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}=4)=\binom{4}{3}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{3} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{4-3}+\binom{4}{4}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{4} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{4-4}=\frac{4 !}{3 ! 1 !} \cdot \frac{8}{27} \cdot \frac{1}{3}+\frac{4 !}{4 ! 0 !} \cdot \frac{16}{81}=\frac{32}{81}+\frac{16}{81}=\frac{48}{81}=\frac{16}{27}$

questions.q: The value of $\mathrm{f}(0)$ so that $\frac{\left(-\mathrme^{\mathrm{x}}+2^{\mathrm{x}}\right)}{\mathrm{x}}$ may be continuous at $x=0$ is
questions.solution:
$f(x)=\frac{-e^{x}+2^{x}}{x}=\frac{1}{x}\left[-\left(1+\frac{x}{1 !}+\frac{x^{2}}{2 !}+\frac{x^{3}}{3 !}+..\right)+1+\frac{\log 2}{1 !} x+\right.\left.\quad \frac{(\operatorname{bg} 2)^{2}}{2 !} x^{2}+\frac{(\log 2)^{3}}{3 !} x^{3}+..\right]\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=& \log 2-1+\frac{\mathrm{x}}{2 !}\left\{(\log 2)^{2}-1\right\} \\
&+\frac{\mathrmx^{2}}{3 !}\left\{\left(\log ^{2}\right)^{3}-1\right\}+\ldots.
\end{aligned}$
Putting $x=0$, we get
$\mathrm{f}(0)=\log 2-1+0+0+\ldots.=-1+\log 2$
